payload.title: Auth & identity hardening: OIDC/SAML, sessions, device binding, password hashing
payload.description:
Close the production gaps in the identity/auth surface. Built today: Apple/Google/email-password providers, sessions, demo auth. Unbuilt/incomplete:

- Generic OIDC / SAML / arbitrary OAuth provider routing (operations.md:274-275; threat-model.md:394; status.md "Generic OIDC, SAML... remain unimplemented").
- Provider sessions use a fixed 30-day lifetime instead of FRICK_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS, and provider + password-reset routes don't share the built-in auth-attempt limiter (threat-model.md:378-379; status.md).
- No server-side device binding — session row carries deviceId/replicaId but trusts client-supplied values (threat-model.md:42-43).
- No refresh-token / short-access-token split; token lifetime is one knob (threat-model.md:44-45).
- No proactive session revocation API — operators can only DELETE rows in SQL (threat-model.md:38-40).
- Password hashing is node:crypto.scrypt; production target is a configurable/pluggable hasher (Argon2/bcrypt) with migration path (threat-model.md:344-349).

Target: unified session TTL + limiter across all providers, generic federation, device-bound tokens, refresh/access split, admin revocation API, pluggable password hashing.
